name: Predator-Prey Chase Waves
desc: A hunt spread across a whole landscape and held still enough to look at — prey breaks out into bright arcs wherever the ground is good, the predator crescent runs each arc down from behind and eats a hole through it, and prey floods back into the emptied hole from the flank, the two populations chasing each other forever as false-colour channels that never once settle.

predation.doc: attack rate — how hard the predator crops the prey; higher = leaner standing crop, sharper crashes, harder-edged fronts

scale.doc: grain of the landscape (higher = fewer, chunkier patches)

speed.doc: how fast the ecology runs (PDE steps per second)

hue.doc: prey pigment hue; the predator channel sits opposite it (exposure is luma-normalised, so any hue holds its key)

style.doc: aesthetic — two-channel fluorescence plate / aerial ecological survey with the predator as advancing shade / pale prey wash under a dark predator flood on toned paper / edge-only radiograph of the fronts alone / ironbow map of total standing biomass

act.doc: multi-minute program — steady pursuit / predation cycling over ~5.7 min / habitat productivity swinging over ~4 min from lean sharp filaments to a lush coarse mosaic

seed.doc: seeds the habitat map and the spiral cores sown into the initial phase field
